# **Wick by Good Question**

**Team:** Chow Shino, Tan Wei Ru

**Problem Statement:** Stress & Workload Manager

**Video Presentation:** https://youtu.be/I2ZqSnP1XYU
**Presentation Slides:** [https://canva.link/igx68dvzlpzs5me](https://canva.link/igx68dvzlpzs5me) 
**Readme docs:** https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cWOPC8SYzWQ8XfaWpm0CMP66rhuChU3gbKqTRK_lPAE/edit?usp=sharing

## **1\. Project Overview**

### **The Problem**

University students rarely burn out because of one big event. It's assignments, part-time work, social commitments, errands and their own physical/mental upkeep all piling on top of each other, quietly, until the pile is too tall to notice. Two things make this specific to students:

* **Load is invisible.** There is no single place a student can look to see "how full is my week right now," so overcommitment happens by default — everyone keeps saying yes until something breaks.  
* **The warning signs are self-reported and easy to ignore.** By the time a student *feels* burnt out, the underlying physiological stress has usually been elevated for days. Nobody is measuring that in real time.

**Stakeholders:** the student carrying the load (primary), their close friend group / course-mates (secondary — burnout is contagious in social circles and peer support is one of the strongest protective factors), and indirectly universities and employers who lose productivity and wellbeing to unmanaged burnout.

**What exists today, and where it falls short:**

| Existing app | What it does | Why it falls short for this problem |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Todoist / Notion-style task managers | Track tasks and deadlines | Show *what* you have to do, never *how much you can actually take* — no capacity model, no physiological signal, no push toward recovery |
| Headspace / Calm | Meditation and guided breathing on demand | Purely reactive — the user has to already know they're stressed and open the app themselves; no passive detection, no workload context |
| Apple Health / Fitbit stress or HRV widgets | Passively measure heart-rate variability | Report a number with no interpretation, no link back to *why* (workload), and no actionable next step — just data, no coaching |

None of these connect **"how loaded am I"** to **"how stressed is my body right now"** to **"what should I actually do about it."** That triangulation is the gap Wick fills.

### **Our Solution**

Wick is a mobile app that fuses three signals which are a **passive workload score** (from calendar \+ tasks), a **physiological stress reading** (from camera-based heart-rate-variability sensing, no wearable needed), and **self-reported check-ins** — into one honest "how full is your week" picture, and then actively pushes the student toward rebalancing and recovery instead of just reporting a number at them.

**Core feature set:**

### **Module 1 — Passive Load Engine**

*Builds the "how full is my week" picture without the student having to log anything extra.*

* Calendar sync (Google Calendar, Outlook) \+ AI task/errand entry  
* NLP Quick-Add — parses casual text like "Exam tomorrow 8am" straight into an accurate, high-priority scheduled commitment  
* Categorised load map across Academic, Social, Physical, Errands, and Mental/downtime  
* Workload Visualiser — a single "You're at 90% capacity this week" dial, broken down by category  
* AI Load Balancer — flags whichever category has spiked and suggests concrete lower-priority tasks to defer

  ### **Module 2 — Desk Mode (ambient stress detection)**

*Reads real physiological stress during a focus session, with no wearable.*

* Interval-sampled remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) via the front camera — short bursts, not continuous streaming — extracting a heart-rate/HRV trend  
* Movement/fidget index as a secondary stress cue, computed honestly from the same signal (a real proxy, not a fabricated posture/jaw-tension claim)  
* Adaptive Pomodoro — break timing shifts based on the live stress trend instead of a fixed 25-minute block  
* Threshold escalation — two consecutive high-stress reads locks the timer into a short guided breathing sequence with no skip button; detection converts directly into an enforced pause  
* White Noise & Soundscapes during focus sessions (rain, ocean, forest, fan)  
* Post-session calibration prompt — "Did that read feel accurate?" — visibly refines personal accuracy over time  
* On-device, discard-immediately processing — nothing raw is ever stored or transmitted  
* 3-second setup check confirming a face is present and well-lit before the timer starts

  ### **Module 3 — Calibration & Ground Truth**

*Makes sure "high stress" means high for you, not against a generic population baseline.*

* Short perceived-stress questionnaire at onboarding sets a personal baseline  
* On-demand rear-camera \+ flashlight finger-PPG spot check for a high-accuracy reading that validates/corrects the rPPG trend  
* 1-tap quick stress flag, available anytime, feeding the same calibration loop  
* Trend Velocity Alert — flags when stress is climbing faster than *your own* historical pattern, catching the silent pile-up before the load score itself looks alarming

  ### **Module 4 — Triangulated Load Score**

*Fuses everything into one number the student can actually trust.*

* Fuses passive calendar/task load, Desk Mode biometric readings, and self-report (questionnaire \+ quick-flags) into a single score  
* Visible confidence indicator based on how many signal types currently agree — a demoable technical differentiator, not a black box  
* Correlates self-reported stress against domain load to surface *which* domain is actually driving the strain, instead of a vague "life in general" reading

  ### **Module 5 — Recovery Engine**

*The direct answer to "shouldn't just track and report" — a closed loop: detect, act, confirm.*

* Category-specific pushes such as stretching slot, an outdoor walk or a breathing pause based on the free slots of the day.  
* Closed-loop confirmation — with location consent, confirms the person actually left the house before marking a recovery block complete  
* **Wick Garden** — an anti-FOMO, non-punitive reward loop: completing a micro-reset or de-stress mini-game earns seeds that grow a relaxing virtual garden. Deliberately **not** a daily streak.  
* Internal de-stress mini-games (e.g. bubble-popping) for a quick, non-competitive reset — the actions that earn Wick Garden seeds

  ### **Module 6 — Circles (social recovery layer)**

*Peer accountability, without ever exposing an individual's raw score.*

* Trusted friend pods joined via a unique invite code  
* High-level traffic-light capacity indicators (green/amber/red) per friend, without leaking sensitive personal schedules or raw scores  
* One-tap word of support or shared-challenge invitation  
* Shared recovery challenges (e.g. a group walk, a screen-free tea break)


## **2\. Ideation & Process**

### **2.1 Ideas We Considered**

| Idea | Why it was dropped / kept |
| :---- | :---- |
| Desk Mode via Phone Camera rPPG & CV (Chosen) | Kept. Solves the fundamental hardware bottleneck by reading heart-rate variability (HRV) and physical stress cues (jaw tension, posture, fidgeting) directly through the front-facing camera during focus sessions. Delivers objective biometric grounding without requiring students to buy expensive wearables. Supports both full sampling for accuracy and an interval battery-saver mode. |
| Triangulated Load Engine with NLP Quick-Add (Chosen) | Kept. Fuses passive calendar/task load, live biometrics, and quick self-reports into a single confidence-weighted score. Integrated natural language processing (NLP) to parse casual text (e.g., *"Exam tomorrow 8am"*) into accurate, high-priority scheduled calendar commitments. |
| Closed-Loop Enforced Recovery & Wick Garden (Chosen) | Kept. Directly fulfills the brief's mandate to push toward recovery rather than passively report burnout. Features adaptive Pomodoro locks, auto-reserved calendar recovery blocks, and an anti-FOMO "Wick Garden" where completing micro-resets and de-stress mini-games yields seeds to nurture a relaxing virtual garden. |
| Circles Social Accountability Layer (Chosen) | Kept. Connects trusted friend pods via unique invite codes. Displays high-level traffic-light capacity indicators (green/amber/red) without leaking sensitive personal schedules, allowing peers to send supportive nudges and participate in shared recovery challenges (e.g., group walks). |
| Smart Wearable Integration (Apple Watch / Garmin / Fitbit) | Dropped. Dropped due to the immense engineering complexity of integrating fragmented, proprietary multi-brand health APIs within a hackathon timeframe, as well as the cost-exclusionary nature of requiring students to own smartbands. |
| Gamified Recovery Streaks | Dropped (Post-Mentorship Pivot). Originally tied daily recovery to a streak counter. Dropped because daily streaks induce toxic productivity, guilt, and FOMO—adding another layer of psychological pressure to already overwhelmed students. Replaced with the ambient, non-punitive Wick Garden seed economy. |
| Campus Pulse (Campus-Wide Institutional Stress Heatmap) | Dropped. Tracking anonymous faculty-wide stress trends proved over-scoped for a 2-person sprint. It also raised institutional data-governance concerns and distracted from the core immediate user feedback loop between individual workload and peer recovery. |
| AI Conversational Coaching Chatbot (Woebot-style) | Dropped. Conversational chatbots often feel robotic, dismissible, and gimmicky when a student is in acute overload. The team prioritized structural schedule rebalancing, automated decline drafting, and enforced downtime pauses over chat advice. |
| Pure Rule-Based Self-Report Tracker (Initial Ballast Concept) | Dropped as a standalone model. Relying solely on manual check-ins and subjective domain weighting suffers from acute logging fatigue and self-assessment bias during crunch periods. Upgraded to feed into the Triangulated Load Score alongside objective biometrics. |

## **3\. Design & Prototype**

**UI Prototype:** \[ [https://goodquestion-wick.expo.app](https://goodquestion-wick.expo.app) \]

***Baseline***

The setup screen that turns "connect your accounts" into a personal calibration. Sync your calendar and Wick pulls in your real week; any new or unclear events go through the NLP Quick-Add review, so you're confirming categorized, scheduled tasks instead of filling out forms. Alongside that, a short five-item perceived-stress questionnaire (adapted from the Perceived Stress Scale) sets your personal baseline on the same 0–100 scale as the biometric and load signals — so later, "high stress" is measured against your normal, not a generic population average. Finish it once and Wick has everything it needs to start reading your week honestly from day one.

***![][image2]![][image3]![][image4]***

***Home Page***

The dashboard that makes your week's load visible at a glance. A capacity ring shows what percentage of your week is booked, broken down by category (Academic, Work, Social, Physical, Mental, Errands) in a stacked bar underneath. If a category spikes, the Smart Load Balancer surfaces specific lower-priority tasks to defer, with one tap to push them to next week. A Quick Add bar lets you type a task in plain language ("Exam tomorrow 8am") and Wick's NLP parses it straight into a correctly categorized, scheduled, prioritized entry — no forms.

![][image5]![][image6]![][image7]

***Recovery Page***

The screen that turns "you're stressed" into an actual break. Wick looks at the real gaps left in today's synced schedule and proposes a plan that fits them — a stretch, an outdoor walk, a breathing pause — timed to slots that genuinely exist, not generic reminders. Starting a plan tracks real progress and only counts it complete (and rewards you) once you actually finish. Completed sessions earn seeds that grow Your Garden — a deliberately non-punitive, no-streaks reward loop you can drag and arrange at your own pace. For a faster reset, Bubble Pop offers a two-minute de-stress mini-game that feeds the same seed economy.

![][image8]![][image9]![][image10]

***Desk mode***

Desk Mode turns focus sessions into live stress readings: as the user works, the front camera periodically senses subtle facial pulse signals (rPPG) and fidget patterns to monitor real-time stress—triggering adaptive breaks or guided micro-resets when tension spikes.![][image11]

***Circles***

Circles enables privacy-preserving social accountability by showing anonymized aggregate friend status ('2 of 3 friends in the Red Zone'), allowing users to send quick supportive nudges ('You got this', 'Take a break'), and join shared recovery challenges (e.g., Group Walk, Screen-Free Tea Break) without exposing personal schedules or individual scores.![][image12]![][image13]

## **4\. What Makes It Different**

| Feature | Existing Solutions (Todoist, Calm, Apple Health) | Wick's Original Twist & Novelty |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Triangulated Stress Grounding** | Either track static tasks or output raw biometric numbers without context. | **Fuses task density \+ on-device biometric cues \+ micro-check-ins.** Evaluates whether biological strain matches schedule volume, displaying a confidence metric rather than an opaque score. |
| **Device-Agnostic Biometrics** | Requires purchasing expensive smartwatches ($200–$500) with fragmented APIs. | **Zero-hardware rPPG.** Uses the student's existing smartphone camera to capture micro-facial color variations (blood volume pulse) and CV posture cues, completely democratizing access. |
| **Intervention Model** | Passive, dismissible notifications (*"Consider taking a break"*), which stressed students routinely ignore. | **Enforced Closed-Loop Recovery.** Locks the session into guided recovery upon high-stress detection. Mostly passive reminders, break suggestions, or wellness prompts that users can dismiss. |
| **Incentive Architecture** | Streak counters that penalize missed days, inadvertently driving guilt, anxiety, and FOMO. | **The Wick Garden.** Replaces stressful streaks with an ambient seed-and-growth model where micro-breaks and calming mini-games nurture virtual plants with zero streak-loss penalties. |
| **Social Layer** | Either non-existent or invasive (broadcasting exact calendars, locations, or raw health data). | **Privacy-Preserving Friend Circles.** Uses simple traffic-light signals via private codes to trigger real-world peer recovery (group walks, check-in nudges) without exposing personal calendars. |

## **5\. Technical Architecture & Feasibility**

**Tech stack**

| Layer | Choice | Rationale & Trade-offs | Constraints & Mitigations |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Mobile Frontend** | **React Native (Expo)** | Cross-platform compatibility across iOS and Android with rapid iteration speed. Provides standard APIs for camera and haptics. | *Constraint:* Native bridge overhead for video processing. *Mitigation:* Process lightweight frames directly using optimized native modules; maintain mock toggles for browser-based judging emulators. |
| **Camera & rPPG** | **react-native-vision-camera 5 frame processor on a worklet thread** | Each frame is reduced inside the worklet to a single number — mean intensity of one colour channel in a fixed ROI (red under torch for finger, green for face). The frame buffer is never copied out, written, or transmitted. | *Constraint:* VisionCamera 5's face detector is iOS-only (createObjectOutput throws on Android), so landmark-based ROI tracking isn't portable.  *Mitigation:* fixed ROI plus a skin-colour presence heuristic — enough to answer "is a skin surface filling the sampling region", which is rPPG's actual precondition. |
| **Signal Processing** | **Custom DSP in ppgService** | Detrend → Butterworth bandpass 0.7–3.5 Hz (42–210 BPM) applied zero-phase via filtfilt → peak detection with sub-sample refinement → inter-beat intervals → RMSSD. Runs entirely on-device. | *Constraint:* a bandpass makes any input oscillate, so noise can masquerade as a pulse.  *Mitigation:* explicit signal-quality gate — IBIs outside 300–2000 ms are discarded and a reading below the quality floor returns poor rather than a fabricated number. |
| **Battery Management** | **Two sensing modes** | Continuous: 40 s analysis window, 15 s stride. Battery-saver: camera open 45 s every 180 s. | *Constraint:* \~12–18%/hr on a mid-range phone for continuous sensing.  *Mitigation:* saver mode costs \~4%/hr; the figure is stated in the UI rather than hidden. |
| **NLP & Quick-Add Engine** | **Regex Parser \+ Lightweight LLM / Compromise NLP** | Extracts entities (dates, times, task labels, course codes) from conversational student text to structure task objects automatically. | *Constraint:* latency, rate limits, offline.  *Mitigation:* every AI path has a deterministic heuristic behind it — the app never blocks on a model, and with no key configured it still parses dates, durations and priorities locally. |
| **Backend & Database** | **Supabase — Postgres, Auth, Row-Level Security, SECURITY DEFINER RPCs** | Handles auth, Circles sync and aggregates. 21 tables, every one RLS-locked to auth.uid(). Privileged reads go through SECURITY DEFINER functions (get\_circle\_summary, send\_circle\_support) so a client can't forge a friendship and start reading. | *Constraint:* free-tier limits.  *Mitigation:* only processed scalars are stored — never raw frames, waveforms or IBI lists; there is deliberately no column for them. The app also runs fully offline against an AsyncStorage store with the same shape. |
| **Calendar Sync** | **Google Calendar API / Device Calendar** | Reads event volume to calculate capacity; writes recovery blocks straight into the user’s real schedule. | *Constraint:* OAuth consent verification and token management in demo builds. *Mitigation:* Support standard device-level calendar access via Expo Calendar, supplemented by seeded mock calendar profiles for instant live judging. |
| **Hosting** | **EAS Hosting (static Expo Router web export); EAS Build for native** | Judge-facing build is live at goodquestion-wick.expo.app. | *Constraint:* no camera or pedometer in a browser.  *Mitigation:* the hosted build ships with no backend keys, so it boots straight into a seeded realistic week — no signup, no setup, nothing to leak. |
